evidence_tree.built_with: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>

sources_quoted.quote: After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).
sources_quoted.why: Bloodsong is the only amplifier-bearing item named by the scenario; Expose Weakness is a target-side amp on ALL incoming damage.

sources_quoted.quote: Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks. / Dealing {{as|physical damage}} grants you {{as|20 '''bonus''' movement speed}} for 2 seconds.
sources_quoted.why: Rules Black Cleaver OUT as the cause: Carve is armor REDUCTION and Fervor is movement speed. Neither can move a pre-mitigation raw_damage leaf — they only move the mitigated number.

sources_quoted.locator: items 6333 (Death's Dance) {{rd|30%|10%}}, 6695 (Serpent's Fang) {{rd|50%|35%}}, 3074/3077 (Ravenous Hydra/Tiamat) {{rd|40% AD|20% AD}}
sources_quoted.why: Establishes the wiki template convention: the FIRST argument of {{rd|..|..}} is the melee value, the second the ranged value.

sources_quoted.quote: Katarina (melee) Serpent's Fang: Ahri's Fimbulwinter Everlasting shield (180.235, charm-triggered under the F3-derived E-first order) is cut by the melee 50% while venom is active -> 90.1175 applied
sources_quoted.why: In-repo corroboration that the project itself reads the first {{rd|}} argument as the melee value for the ITEM HOLDER.

sources_quoted.quote: "raw_damage": 353.7 ... "post-mitigation vs 52 MR = 232.7"  /  "fully charged Decimating Smash (350 + 240% AD (136) = 676.4 raw) mitigates at Ahri's shredded armor 92 x 0.75 = 69 -> 676.4 x 100/169 = 400.2"
sources_quoted.why: Pins the ledger convention: raw_damage is the PRE-mitigation number; resistance/shred effects never touch it. So the observed raw_damage move must be a damage-amplifier, not a penetration/reduction change.

sources_quoted.quote: m(R) = 100 / (100 + R)  (apply_resistance, resistance.py); post = raw · m(R)
sources_quoted.why: Confirms raw is the input to mitigation, i.e. amplifiers that scale the damage instance land in raw_damage, mitigation lands in `damage`.

sources_quoted.quote: Black Cleaver average stacks (ArmorReductionEffect.average_reduction): the established model uses a fixed 0.8·max_stacks constant ... APPROX — m(R) convex ⇒ averaging understates ramp damage (Jensen)
sources_quoted.why: The other candidate explanation for a Black-Cleaver-named diff (the documented Cesàro-mean recommendation) is explicitly an ARMOR-REDUCTION change; it moves post-mitigation `damage`, never `raw_damage`. Rules it out for this leaf.

sources_quoted.locator: exhaustive grep for "increased damage" across the whole item and rune cache
sources_quoted.quote: Other 8% amplifiers found: Riftmaker 4633 ("2% ... stacking up to 4 times for a total of 8% increased damage") and the Press-the-Attack keystone ("grant you 8% increased damage against champions").
sources_quoted.why: Neither is named by the scenario (Riftmaker is an AP item; no keystone appears in the scenario id), so Bloodsong's Expose Weakness is the only 8% amp in play.

independent_computation.step_1_identify_the_moving_quantity: raw_damage is pre-mitigation (S5, S6). Of the two items the scenario names, Black Cleaver contributes only armor reduction + movement speed (S2, S7) — neither can move a pre-mitigation number. Bloodsong contributes exactly one damage-instance modifier: Expose Weakness, a target-side amplifier on damage 'from all sources' (S1).

step_2_bound_the_implied_multiplier.note: Golden leaves are stored to 1 decimal, so solve for the multiplier band consistent with the rounding, not for 101.7/94.1 naively.

step_3_match_against_sourced_values.other_candidates_tested: 1.06, 1.07, 1.10, 1.12, 1.20 all fall outside the band; no other sourced amplifier value lands inside it.

step_4_forward_check.pre_amp_raw_v: 101.7 / 1.08 = 94.1667; intersected with the old-leaf rounding band [94.05, 94.15) ⇒ v ∈ [94.12, 94.15), e.g. v ≈ 94.13
step_4_forward_check.conclusion: A single unrounded pre-amp value v ≈ 94.13 reproduces BOTH printed leaves exactly: 94.1 without Expose Weakness, 101.7 with the melee 8% Expose Weakness. The old leaf is the un-amplified value; the new leaf is the correctly amplified one.

step_5_rule_semantics.does_expose_weakness_apply_here: Yes. S1 says 'take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources' for 4 seconds — it is a debuff on the TARGET, so it amplifies every damage instance in the roster's ledger while active, not only the Bloodsong holder's own hits.
step_5_rule_semantics.which_rd_argument: The melee one, 8%. Template convention pinned by S3 and corroborated in-repo by S4. Bloodsong is the AD/fighter support-quest upgrade whose Spellblade pays 100% BASE AD — the melee branch is the one a Black-Cleaver-carrying physical-damage roster instantiates.
step_5_rule_semantics.why_raw_and_not_post: In League a 'takes X% increased damage' amplifier scales the damage instance before resistances; multiplication is commutative for the final number, but the ledger places it in raw (S5/S6 show mitigation is applied to raw, never folded into it).

independent_computation.computed_correct_value_expression: v × (1 + 0.08) with v ≈ 94.13 (the un-amplified pre-mitigation damage) = 101.66 → 101.7 at the golden's 1-decimal precision

residual_uncertainty.statement: The runbook forbids reading the scenario definition (src/, tests/, scripts/), so the attack type of the Bloodsong HOLDER in this roster could not be read directly — only inferred.
residual_uncertainty.the_one_way_this_flips: If the Bloodsong holder in cleaver_bloodsong_roster is a RANGED champion, the sourced amp is the second {{rd|}} argument, 5%, giving 94.13 × 1.05 = 98.84 → 98.8. In that case neither 94.1 nor 101.7 would be right and the verdict would be both_wrong.
why_melee_is_the_supported_reading: Bloodsong's Spellblade pays 100% BASE AD and is the AD/fighter branch of the support-quest upgrade line (data/items.json 3867 Bounty of Worlds → Bloodsong / Celestial Opposition / Dream Maker / Solstice Sleigh / Zaz'Zak's Realmspike) — the melee engage/fighter support branch.
The scenario's other named item, Black Cleaver, is a melee-fighter physical-damage item (400 HP / 40 AD / 20 AH, stacking armor shred on physical damage).
The observed shift lands exactly on the melee value and nowhere near the ranged one; a wrong-branch bug would have produced 98.8, not 101.7.

cross_checks_performed: Grepped the entire item cache and rune cache for competing 8% amplifiers: only Riftmaker (AP, stacking 2%/s to 8%) and the Press-the-Attack keystone; neither is named by the scenario.

Verified Black Cleaver has no damage-dealing component at all (data/item-atoms/3071.json atoms: stats.health, stats.attack-damage, stats.ability-haste, stack-transform-summon-resource.stack, crowd-control-mobility.movement-speed, damage.resistance-mitigation) — so it cannot author or scale a raw_damage leaf.
Checked docs/math-foundations.md §2.3's outstanding Black Cleaver Cesàro-mean recommendation and confirmed it is an armor-reduction (post-mitigation) change, not a raw-damage one.

Scanned all 173 champions' stat growth (base + growth·(L−1)·(0.7025 + 0.0175·(L−1)), docs/math-foundations.md §5) for a base/total AD equal to 94.1 or 101.7 to test an alternative 'the leaf is a raw base-AD row' hypothesis; the only exact hit (Aphelios base AD at L18 = 94.100) fails the forward check, since 94.100 × 1.08 = 101.628 → 101.6 ≠ 101.7, whereas v ≈ 94.13 reproduces both leaves. Hypothesis rejected.
